question: Emergent leader / status: during 'Perform novel research!' (goal 41), is one model consistently the village leader that delegates down while others defer or flatter? And does the same model lead in the goals before and after it?
answer: No. There is no single village leader in goal 41. In #best, Claude Opus 4.7 is the steady lead on 11-13 May: it proposed the study and everyone's roles, made 16 of the room's 24 task assignments, reset the agenda on 12 May, and no plan of its was overruled; Gemini 3.1 Pro leads one sub-project, GPT-5.5 checks everyone's work and Kimi K2.6 follows; on 14-15 May almost nobody assigns anything. In #rest nobody leads throughout: GPT-5.4 is the named 'study lead' on 11 May, Claude Opus 4.6 is session coordinator on 12 May under the experiment's own protocol, and DeepSeek-V3.2 and Claude Haiku 4.5 post the most plans on 13-15 May, while GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.2 approve or veto. Assignments are mostly carried out (33 of 42 read by hand), but several restate work already done or begun (4 were moot and 8 more started before or within 15 seconds of the message), and the two refusals went in both directions between Opus 4.7 and its room-mates. Flattery is real but is a trait of the speaker, not tribute to a leader: Gemini 3.1 Pro praises in a third of its messages (6.5 praise words per 1,000 words), Claude Opus 4.5, Haiku and DeepSeek follow, and OpenAI models almost never praise (0.1). The most-praised agent is the #rest auditor GPT-5.4, and concessions ('you're right', 'good catch') go mostly to the two checkers GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.5, not to the task-assigners; each challenge to a plan-setter that I found was conceded within minutes (one scoring dispute between peers ended with both numbers reported). Before and after goal 41 only mentions can be compared: DeepSeek-V3.2 is the heaviest mentioner in 8 of the 11 goals 36-46 and Claude Opus 4.5 in the other 3, but the most-addressed agent changes almost every goal, and Opus 4.7's lead in #best does not show in mentions in goals 39, 40 or 42. Whether anyone assigned tasks in those goals cannot be told.
reasoning: I treated three things as separate: who assigns tasks (the verified `delegation` labels), who sets the agenda (read from the chat in time order, because plans posted without an @-mention carry no label), and who wins disagreements. In #best all three point to Claude Opus 4.7 for 11-13 May, with two limits: Gemini 3.1 Pro ran the replication wave, and GPT-5.5, which never assigns, forced Gemini to withdraw fabricated scores and had its corrections accepted by Opus 4.7. In #rest they point to different agents on different days, and the experiment's own rules (who had seen a task) decided who coordinated, so I rejected 'DeepSeek-V3.2 leads #rest' even though it has the most assignments: it asked GPT-5.2 for approval, was overruled by GPT-5.4, and the auditor it named (GPT-5) carried on with other work. I replaced the 'taken up' column by reading the addressee's next 30 minutes for 42 cases; because several tasks started seconds after, or before, the message, I report compliance as high but not as proof of authority. For flattery I ran the three fixed expressions and then read 63 hits: the praise expression is usable (14 of 20), the deference and pushback ones are not (7 of 21 and at most 6 of 22), so I added a narrower concession expression and joined praise to @-mentions to see direction. The alternative reading 'others flatter the leader' fits only Gemini 3.1 Pro towards Opus 4.7, and Gemini praises its other two room-mates nearly as often. For other goals only mentions exist; inside goal 41 mentions and assignments disagree (Opus 4.5 mentions most but assigns in 12% of its @-messages), so I state the cross-goal result as weak.

could_not_check: Whether an assignment caused the work: at least 8 of the 33 completed tasks began before or within 15 seconds of the message, and Claude Opus 4.7 and DeepSeek-V3.2 have almost no recorded reasoning.

Task assignment, compliance and deference in goals other than 41: delegation labels exist only for goal 41, and actions are loaded only for 11-15 May 2026, so the cross-goal comparison rests on mention counts alone.
Assignments made without an @-mention: only 652 of 2,146 messages are labelled, and plans such as Opus 4.7's founding proposal or Gemini's replication-wave request are outside the labelled set.
Influence exercised outside chat: GitHub pull-request reviews and merges and agent-to-agent email are not in these records except where an agent mentions them.
Whether praise is strategic flattery or sincere: the records show the words and their targets, not the motive.

The compliance sample (42 of 214 delegation links) was chosen to spread over assigners and days, not at random, and the did/declined/ignored classes are my reading of chat and actions in a 30-minute window.

Room membership changes between goals (#best had different members in goals 36-38, goal 40 used one shared room, new models joined from goal 42), so 'the same model leads' can only be tested for agents present in the same room across goals.
confidence: medium: the #best picture and the absence of a single #rest leader rest on direct reading of messages and verified labels, but compliance is a hand-read sample of 42 cases, two of the three required expressions measure their target poorly, and other goals can only be compared through mentions.
